column1: # Hindi minimal pairs - reviewed and curated
# Source: candidates auto-extracted from UD Hindi-HDTB (see hindi_minimal_pairs_candidates.tsv),
# corrected and re-categorized following native-speaker review (2026-07-25).
# Changes from the raw candidate set:
#   - Removed proper nouns/place names (Asia, India, Korea, Shah Jahan, Qudsia, Gohar, Khilji, Charles, Monday)
#   - Deduplicated words that appeared under two conflicting categories (begam, dvaar)
#   - Moved English loanwords out of base_noun/oblique_case_form/plural_form into borrowed_form
#   - Reassigned oblique_case_form entries that were actually direct/citation forms to base_noun
#   - Split plural_form into plural_form_direct vs plural_form_oblique (-on marking)
#   - Split out pronoun_oblique_form and verb_participle_form from the noisy honorific_form bucket
#   - Dropped bare verb stems, a genitive postposition, and other pattern-matching false positives
#     (utha, ja, kar, le, niji, ke, fauji) that did not belong in any category
# Open design question (not yet resolved): several verb_inflection_chain entries are honorific
# imperatives (lijiye, lagaiyega, bhooliyega, uthaiyega, jaiye) - flag for future cross-referencing
# with honorific_form rather than duplicating rows across categories.
# NOTE: only one genuine oblique form survived review. This category needs fresh,
# purpose-built examples (case-inflected forms before postpositions, e.g. ghar -> ghar mein)
# rather than more treebank extraction - the extraction heuristic could not reliably find these.
